Next, the surgery type includes various procedures like gastrectomy, liver resection, Whipple procedure, etc. I'll list them as "Gastrectomy, Liver resection, Whipple, Hemicolectomy, Rectum resection, Radical cystectomy or prostatectomy, Radical resection for gynecologic cancer, Other oncologic resection procedure" from the Methods under the Participants section.

For laparoscopy rates, the study reports 38% in GDFT and 62% in control. These values are from Table 2 under General characteristics.

ASA physical status distribution is also provided in Table 2. GDFT has 6 (12%) ASA I, 36 (72%) ASA II, and 8 (16%) ASA III. Control has 8 (16%) ASA I, 33 (66%) ASA II, and 9 (18%) ASA III.

Total fluid administered is mentioned in the Results under Intraoperative fluid management. GDFT group had a net fluid of 1975 ml (1474–2600), while control had 2906 ml (2250–3300).

Crystalloid and colloid use: GDFT used 1600 ml (913–2100) crystalloids and 500 ml (500–1000) colloids. Control used 2200 ml (2025–2513) crystalloids and 500 ml (0–1000) colloids, as per Table 3.

Blood loss is the same for both groups, 100 ml (0–350), from Table 3.

Inotrope use: GDFT had 27 (54%) patients using inotropes, while control had 18 (36%). This is from Table 3.

Morbidity events: GDFT had 6 (12%) and control had 13 (26%) complications, excluding POGD. This data is in Table 5.

Mortality: Both groups had 0 deaths, as per Table 5.

Hospital LOS: GDFT had 9.0 ±5.8 days, control had 12.0 ±4.6 days, from Results.

Time to flatus: GDFT 28.2 h (9.2–48.0), control 39.4 h (24.9–67.5), from Table 4.

Time to oral intake: GDFT 4.0 days (2.7–6.0), control 6.0 days (5.0–9.3), Table 4.

Time to defecation isn't mentioned, so NR.

Postop ileus (POGD): GDFT 2/50 (4%), control 16/50 (32%), from Results.

I'll structure all this into the JSON format, ensuring each field has the correct value and where it was taken from.
